svg.text: How Carl Ianne's Spending Tracker Works
Read from top to bottom. Part 1 happens once when the app opens. Part 2 repeats every time the user taps something.
Gray box = which files do the work
From opening the website to seeing the first screen
START: the user opens the app
The website is hosted on Vercel. It can also be
installed like a normal app with the Install button.
1. The browser loads the app files
It downloads the page (index.html), the looks (styles.css)
and the JavaScript files. A header from Vercel only allows
files from our own site, so outside scripts are blocked.
This is the page skeleton: a menu, a + button, a
pop-up form and an empty area where screens
It connects the Install button and the + form, builds the
lookup table of button names, and gets ready to load
main.js is the conductor: it only connects the
other files, it does not do the math itself.
store.js asks db.js to read every record and setting from
IndexedDB, the database inside the browser. models.js
checks each record and drops any that are broken. Then
main.js asks the browser not to delete this data.
Nothing is sent to a server.
It can fail in private mode or when an
Show "Can't open your data" with the reason.
The app stops here so nothing is lost or broken.
router.js reads the address (like #/budget) and picks a
view. The view asks calc.js for totals, budget status and
the projection, then builds the HTML. Last, main.js
registers sw.js so the app works offline.
Screens are small files, one per page: Home,
calc.js only does math. It never touches the
PART 2: EVERY TIME THE USER DOES SOMETHING (repeats forever)
The same loop runs for every tap, edit, import or export
Tap +, edit or delete a record, set a budget, change the
month, switch theme, or import or export a file.
Every button carries a name, like
main.js reads the button's name and looks it up in a Map.
If the name is unknown, the console prints a warning
A test fails if any button has no handler, so typos
months and imported files. Actions with
no input go straight to YES.
Examples of what gets rejected: amount of 0 or
less, a date like Feb 30, a month like 2026-13, a
file that is not a real backup.
store.js saves it with db.js (all-or-nothing, so a failure
cannot leave half-saved data), then updates its own copy
settings all use this same path.
store.js announces "data changed". The current view
runs again with the new numbers: balance, budget alerts,
Because the screen is rebuilt from the data every
time, it can never show old numbers.
Four things that happen around the main loop
sw.js keeps a copy of every app file. With no internet the app still opens
and saves, because the data is already on the device.
JSON is a full backup that can be imported back. CSV and Excel are export
only. Home reminds you to back up after 14 days.
A backup file is checked record by record and bad rows are skipped.
"Replace" swaps the records in one step, so a failure keeps the old data.
All typed text is escaped before it reaches the page. Tests and the linter
run on every push (CI), so a break is caught before it goes live.
The dot color matches the step colors above

the current data, save, tell the screens
all the math (no screen, no database)
